title: Slider Bar
subtitle: Mini burgers, max variety
description: Mini burgers, max variety. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Small dome lids for melting cheese

steps.title: Form mini patties
steps.instruction: Divide ground beef into 2-ounce portions (about 32–36 patties for a full hall). Roll gently into balls, then flatten into thin patties slightly wider than the buns — they shrink on the griddle. Indent the center with your thumb so they cook flat.

steps.title: Season and griddle in batches
steps.instruction: Season patties with salt and pepper. Griddle over medium-high 2–3 minutes per side until browned and 160°F. Work in batches so the griddle stays hot — crowded patties steam.

steps.title: Melt cheese on patties
steps.instruction: Top each patty with American cheese in the last minute; cover with a dome lid or foil tent until melted. Transfer finished sliders to sheet trays in a warm oven at 200°F.

steps.title: Toast buns
steps.instruction: Butter cut slider buns and toast cut-side down on the griddle until golden. Pile toasted bottoms and tops in separate foil-lined pans.

steps.title: Build the toppings bar
steps.instruction: Line up lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, ketchup, mustard, and mayo in labeled bowls with tongs and spoons. Put cold toppings on ice if service runs past an hour.

steps.title: Serve build-your-own sliders
steps.instruction: Crew grabs a bottom bun, adds patty with cheese, builds toppings, and caps with the top bun. Hall Slider Bar feeds 8–12 hungry firefighters when you have enough buns and patties — plan seconds before the line opens.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Line mini patties with cheese on sheet trays; toasted buns split into top and bottom pans.
Build toppings bar in order: lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, then ketchup, mustard, and mayo at the end.
Plan 3–4 sliders per firefighter — count buns before the line opens so nobody gets shorted.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Mini burgers, max variety. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free bun/bread and toast on a separate, clean surface.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a dairy-free cheese shred/block alternative. Use a plant-based butter/margarine.
